questions.prompt: Is there a defect in how this code resolves which API version a request uses? If so, mark the line(s) where it is; otherwise answer that there is none.
A client sends the header `Accept-Version: V2 ` (capital V, trailing space) with `q=wifi`. What does it receive?
choices: A 400 response, because only lowercase `v` prefixes are accepted
A 200 response in the version 2 shape, with `API-Version: 2`
A 200 response in the version 3 shape, because the value is not purely numeric
A 200 response in the version 1 shape with Deprecation headers

questions.prompt: Why does _respond add `Vary: Accept-Version` to every response?
choices: It tells browsers to refuse to send the header on cross-origin requests
It makes the server reject requests whose version differs from the previous one
It declares that the same URL can return different bodies depending on the header, so shared caches must key on it
It marks responses as deprecated so clients migrate

questions.prompt: A developer adds `_shape_v4` and registers it as `SHAPERS[4]`, but does not touch SUPPORTED_VERSIONS. A client sends `Accept-Version: 4`. What happens?
choices: The request is served by _shape_v3 because 4 is not a supported version
The server raises KeyError because SHAPERS and SUPPORTED_VERSIONS disagree
The request gets a 400 `unsupported_version` response listing versions 1 to 3
